query: Earlier studies of conventional metallic multilayers provide a general framework for deformation, but its conclusions may not transfer directly to high-entropy-alloy systems because compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order are associated with unusual deformation behavior. Preliminary evidence from FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers remains insufficient to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates. Within the constraints of retaining a nanoscale multilayer coating and balancing strength with deformation tolerance, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading? State what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would expose it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, boundary conditions, relevant prior support, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: At intermediate homologous temperatures (≈0.35–0.6 T_m) the steady-state creep of nanoscale FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy (HEA) multilayer coatings is governed by interface-controlled diffusional flow that is rate-limited by vacancy-assisted dislocation climb at chemically disordered, coherency-strained interfaces. Because the number of such interfaces per unit volume grows as the bilayer period decreases, multilayers with thinner periods will creep faster (higher steady-state strain-rate at a given stress) than otherwise identical films with thicker periods, despite their higher initial yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Sputter-deposited [FCC HEA/BCC HEA]n multilayer coating, overall thickness 2–5 µm, columnar grains aligned normal to the substrate; two sets of bilayer periods: 5 nm and 50 nm; average room-temperature hardness ≈10 GPa.
generation.intervention: Apply a constant uniaxial (or indentation) stress equal to 0.4 σ_y while holding the sample at 0.45 T_m for 10 h.
generation.conditions: Vacuum or inert atmosphere to suppress oxidation; temperature ±2 K; stress held constant to ±2 %.
generation.structural_mediator: Semi-coherent FCC|BCC interfaces that contain high local lattice distortion and short-range chemical order, which act as high-density vacancy sources/sinks and fast diffusion ‘pipes’.
generation.mechanism: Stress-assisted vacancy generation/absorption at the chemically disordered interfaces enables dislocation climb across layers. Interface sliding accommodated by climb produces out-of-plane shear step accumulation, giving macroscopic plastic strain. The rate is proportional to interface area density, so thinner bilayer periods accelerate creep.
generation.predicted_outcome: At identical stress and temperature the 5 nm-period multilayer will show a steady-state creep rate at least one order of magnitude higher than the 50 nm-period multilayer (e.g., 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹ vs 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹). Activation volume extracted from stress-jump tests will be ~10–20 b³, characteristic of climb-controlled rather than glide-controlled flow.
generation.baseline: In conventional metallic multilayers (e.g., Cu/Nb) and in the same HEA multilayers tested at room temperature, creep rate decreases or remains unchanged as bilayer period is reduced because dislocation glide or confined layer slip dominates.
generation.boundary: Effect expected only for 0.35 T_m ≤ T ≤ 0.6 T_m, stresses below ~0.6 σ_y, and bilayer periods ≤100 nm. At lower T or higher stresses where glide is activated, or for periods >100 nm where interface density is low, the trend should revert or vanish.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the rate increase (one order of magnitude) is estimated; actual value may vary with specific alloy chemistry or residual defects.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two otherwise identical HEA multilayer coatings with 5 nm and 50 nm bilayer periods. Measure their constant-load creep in a nanoindenter equipped with heating stage at 0.45 T_m. Record depth vs time for 10 h and perform stress-relaxation steps to extract activation volumes.
measurements: Post-test TEM/EDS to confirm interface structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (a) ε̇_ss for the 5 nm period is ≤ ε̇_ss for the 50 nm period, or (b) activation volume greatly exceeds ~50 b³ (indicative of bulk glide) for both periods.
